answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked, attested identity. Each agent entering through the inlet locks collateral and gathers signed uniqueness vouchers from peers, becoming a trusted vertex in a web-of-trust graph. Rewards (the nectar) flow only to vertices with enough independent attestations, so one operator spawning fakes gains no extra share: every fake vertex needs its own bond and vouchers. The attacker pays collateral per forged identity, and when peers flag the duplicate cluster the whole stake is slashed, making a Sybil army cost more than it could steal.
